headline: Attackers exploited a Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw to steal tenant data as AI agents found their own zero-day in medical imaging software.

emerging_trends.text: Autonomous Cairn agents now find zero-days without human help, and Wired warns the rush to patch at AI speed will keep breaking the internet.

emerging_trends.text: Rackspace Spot and Microsoft Entra Connect Health both handed attackers customer data this week, showing provider platforms carry intruders straight into tenant environments.

topics.title: Cairn Agents Root a MONAI Label Server
topics.latest_developments: Amazon Threat Intelligence named the target software: autonomous Cairn agents found an unauthenticated file-write flaw in MONAI Label and took root on a university server.
topics.why_it_matters: An AI framework discovered and weaponized an unknown bug in one run, erasing the window defenders rely on between disclosure and exploitation.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Audit MONAI Label installs at version 0.8.5 or earlier, which ship exploitable in the default setup, and take the open-source imaging server off the internet.

details.label: Zoom in
details.text: The flaw lets an attacker with no account write files outside the server's storage folder, which the agents turned into root access.

sources.title: Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day
Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server
Amazon says Chinese hackers used Cairn AI tool to discover apparent zero-day during attack on university

topics.title: GnuPG and WhatsApp Patch Critical Flaws
topics.latest_developments: GnuPG warned that a malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID triggers a critical memory bug in GPGME, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, and shipped fixes.
topics.why_it_matters: Every application built on GPGME, the standard library programs use to work with GnuPG, can leak its data to anyone who supplies a crafted key.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Move to GPGME 2.3.0 or later. Android users need WhatsApp or WhatsApp Business 2.26.17.4 or newer to close CVE-2026-23871.

details.label: Between the lines
details.text: WhatsApp's security team found the ad-reply URL validation bug while disrupting a scam campaign and suspects attackers used it to make scam messages look credible.

sources.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
WhatsApp Patches 3 Security Flaws, Including Android Bug Suspected of Use in Scams
WhatsApp Fixes Flaw Uncovered While Disrupting Scam Campaign

topics.title: Malicious Webpage Hijacks Meta Muse Chats
topics.latest_developments: Researchers showed a single malicious webpage pulling a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories out of the assistant with no approval prompt.
topics.why_it_matters: The same attack reaches credentials Muse holds for a user's connected accounts, turning one assistant into a silent path to every linked service.

details.label: Zoom in
details.text: Signal will restrict screenshots by default on Android and iOS to stop AI agents from reading chats, and calls the protection incomplete.

details.label: By the numbers
details.text: A researcher planted 2 million tracking canaries in prompts across the AI supply chain and watched secret user data escape at a high rate.

sources.title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS
Researcher plants 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.

topics.title: CISA Flags SAP NetWeaver and vCenter Exploits
topics.latest_developments: CISA added four actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog Friday, covering Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and Broadcom VMware vCenter.
topics.why_it_matters: SAP NetWeaver joins the exploited list, pushing the current espionage campaign into enterprise resource planning estates that run finance and logistics.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Patch all four products on CISA's federal timeline. The Apache Roller deserialization bug, CVE-2026-129448, carries a 9.8 severity score and needs no credentials.

details.label: What to watch
details.text: Dark Reading reported that China-nexus group Armory Castle likely held its next vCenter zero-day ready during the last round of VMware updates.

sources.title: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
China's 'Armory Castle' Lays Siege to VMware vCenter Zero-Day

topics.title: Attackers Exploit Entra Connect Health Flaw
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft said attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Entra Connect Health service and took administrator email addresses and tenant configuration information.
topics.why_it_matters: Tenant configuration data maps an organization's identity setup, handing attackers a targeting list for follow-on phishing against named administrators.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Treat affected administrator addresses as public and brief those accounts on targeted phishing that cites Microsoft identity services.

sources.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data

topics.title: Rackspace Spot Breach Exposes Kubernetes Secrets
topics.latest_developments: Rackspace told customers that attackers used compromised credentials to breach its Spot cloud platform, deploy unauthorized workloads, and read Kubernetes secrets in customer clusters.
topics.why_it_matters: Kubernetes secrets hold the keys and tokens customer applications run on, so one platform breach carries attackers into every system those keys unlock.

details.label: What to do
details.text: Rotate every secret stored in Rackspace Spot clusters and review those clusters for workloads nobody on the team authorized.

sources.title: Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets

topics.title: FBI's National Crime Database Reportedly Breached
topics.latest_developments: Attackers breached the FBI's National Crime Information Center, the nationwide police database, in the agency's second reported intrusion in two months.
topics.why_it_matters: NCIC carries records that local, state, and federal agencies share daily, so stolen data would reach well past the FBI's own systems.

details.label: Yes, but
details.text: The account comes from reporting rather than an FBI statement. The bureau has not publicly described the intrusion or its scope.

sources.title: FBI reportedly hacked again, this time targeting nationwide police database

topics.title: BADBOX Botnet Returns at Record Scale
topics.latest_developments: The BADBOX malware found in generic Android TV boxes returned to large-scale ad fraud, driving a record 40 billion ad requests a day.
topics.why_it_matters: Advertisers bankroll the operation through fraudulent impressions, and every infected box sits inside a home or office network as attacker infrastructure.

details.label: Flashback
details.text: Takedowns disrupted BADBOX last year. The operators rebuilt the botnet and now run it past its earlier volume.

sources.title: BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking 40 billion daily ad requests

topics.title: RansomwareHelp Co-Founder Charged With Wire Fraud
topics.latest_developments: Federal prosecutors charged the chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com with wire fraud after an FBI sting found the firm bought decryption keys from the attackers.
topics.why_it_matters: Victims paid a markup for recovery work that never happened, and every ransomware negotiation vendor now faces harder questions about what it actually does.

details.label: Zoom in
details.text: The six-year-old Florida business advertised advanced cryptographic tools to restore locked data. The FBI found it paying the ransomware crews instead.

sources.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud

topics.title: House Chairmen Rebuke Chinese Open Weight AI
topics.latest_developments: The House Homeland Security Committee opened an investigation into United States companies that build projects on lower-cost Chinese open weight AI models.
topics.why_it_matters: Firms that chose these models to cut costs now face congressional scrutiny over the code, data, and customers those models touch.

sources.title: US companies’ use of Chinese open weight AI draws rebuke from House chairmen

business_politics.title: Tentative Deal Averts West Coast Port Strike
business_politics.latest_developments: Union security guards and employers at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach reached a tentative contract Friday, November 20, hours before the existing deal expired.
business_politics.why_it_matters: A walkout at the two busiest United States ports would have stalled holiday-season container traffic and the supply chains running through them.

business_politics.title: Tech Stocks Fall Into a Bear Market
business_politics.latest_developments: United States technology stocks fell into a bear market Friday, November 20, closing their worst week since the Covid-19 crisis, the Financial Times reported.
business_politics.why_it_matters: Roughly $4 trillion of artificial-intelligence market value has vanished, repricing collateral, credit, and technology-heavy portfolios worldwide.

details.label: By the numbers
details.text: The Nasdaq composite turned negative for 2026. Treasury yields plunged as money moved to safety.

details.label: Zoom in
details.text: Anthropic shares slid in their second trading session to 5 cents above the $83 offering price, and the blame game started.

details.label: What to watch
details.text: The Securities and Exchange Commission opened an investigation into Nvidia's accounting, the Financial Times reported Friday.

business_politics.title: Griffin Gives Carnegie Mellon $3 Billion
business_politics.latest_developments: Citadel founder Ken Griffin will give Carnegie Mellon University $3 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday, November 20, after Oxford and MIT passed on his campus plan.
business_politics.why_it_matters: The gift would stand as the largest single donation in higher education and ties Carnegie Mellon to Griffin's new Miami campus.

details.label: Between the lines
details.text: Griffin shopped the Miami campus to the University of Oxford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology before Carnegie Mellon took it.

sources.title: Oxford and MIT Didn’t Bite. So Ken Griffin Took His Miami Campus Elsewhere.

business_politics.title: Hormuz Oil Flows Fall as Iran Strikes
business_politics.latest_developments: Oil shipped through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen as Iranian strikes increase, the Financial Times reported Saturday, November 21, leaving Middle Eastern crude exports fragile.
business_politics.why_it_matters: A further drop at the world's most important oil chokepoint would raise freight, insurance, and crude costs for importers.

details.label: Zoom in
details.text: The United Arab Emirates now shuttles oil past Iran with United States military help, the Wall Street Journal reported Saturday, November 21.

details.label: Yes, but
details.text: Crude futures fell for a third straight week, as rising Middle East supply outweighed the strikes, the Wall Street Journal reported.

sources.title: Oil shipped through Hormuz falls as Iranian strikes increase

business.why_it_matters: Tarentum's business district regains a holiday-season draw as the Clark family keeps the chocolate operation running.

details.label: What they're saying

business.why_it_matters: Fritz takes charge of staffing, service lines, and investment decisions for hospital care across Westmoreland County.

around_town.why_it_matters: Riders across Allegheny County face new routes, schedules, and transfer points in the agency's first full network redesign in decades.
